questions.text: The old colour is shut down 30 minutes after the switch, and the lock is held for that whole time. If a run's step 13 shutdown happens at T0+30, what does 'the new colour is normally shut down when a deploy starts' mean for the first deploy ever, when no colour has been tagged yet?
questions.about: Terms and decisions / Step 3

questions.text: In step 6, what actually starts the 4 instances and where does the new release's code come from? Is it the artifact from step 2 pulled onto instances by some tool, and what is the 'start request' that begins the 10-minute clock?
questions.about: 6. Start the new release in the idle colour

questions.text: Step 5 applies migrations before the new instances exist and before the gates pass. If the new release later aborts, the old release keeps running on the migrated database. How does the old release stay safe if, say, a new table or column is added that it doesn't know about? Is 'additive' the only protection?
questions.about: 5. Apply migrations, once

questions.text: What is the 10-minute deadline's relation to the smoke suite in step 8? If health gate takes 5 minutes, the suite gets only the remaining time. Who decides how long the suite takes, and what is in it?
questions.about: 8. Smoke test suite

questions.text: In step 11, how does the run get the 5xx rate when the switch is instant and the new instances had no public traffic before? What is a 'breach' exactly: one window above 1% at any minute check, or several in a row?
questions.about: 11. Watch the 5xx rate for 15 minutes

questions.text: What does 'the pipeline retries it automatically' mean when a run dies mid-watch or mid-hold, and does the retry still hold the lock? How does it know which step to resume at from tags and the listener alone?
questions.about: 11. Watch the 5xx rate / 12. Hold the old colour untouched

questions.text: The rollback job runs outside the lock. If an engineer rolls back during the hold, what happens to the still-running deploy run at step 12 and 13, and what tags does the rollback job write? Step 13 only checks the listener, so does it end as 'deployed'?
questions.about: Rollback jobs: Rollback while the old colour is still running

questions.text: Who gets paged, and who is 'the owner'? What does the engineer on the receiving end do first when a page arrives with the listener and tags in a mixed state?
questions.about: Fails (deploy alert channel) / Step 5 'Pages the owner'

answers.text: On the first deploy ever no tags exist. Step 3 tags the live group status=live, release=unknown and continues; the other colour must still have 0 instances. Added to the terms.

The pipeline sends a start request, an API call to the platform's instance launcher naming the step 2 artifact SHA; that call is what starts the 10-minute clock. Which launcher tool and how it pulls the artifact is not known, so it is listed under Open questions.

Additive-only is the protection, enforced twice: the step 4 static check rejects drops, renames, type changes and NOT NULL without default, so the old code just ignores new tables and columns and its inserts still work. Added one sentence to step 4.

The health gate and smoke suite share the one 10-minute budget, so the suite gets whatever time is left, and is killed at the deadline. The suite's contents and duration are not known to me; it is an existing suite that the owner of catalog-web decides. Listed under Open questions.

Right after the switch the new instances get public traffic, and the rate is computed from the new target group's load balancer metrics for that traffic only. A breach is one evaluation above 1% over a trailing 5-minute window at any minute check, with no need to repeat, matching the requirement. Both are now written in the document.

The retry is the pipeline's automatic job retry of the same run, so it keeps the lock; that platform behaviour is assumed, not verified (listed as open). It picks the step from the listener plus switched_at in the tags: under 15 minutes since switch resumes at step 11, under 30 at step 12, otherwise step 13.

The rollback job writes the restored group status=live and the group taken out of service status=rolled_back, like 11a. The deploy run's step 13 sees the old group is live and skips shutdown, and step 14 reports the outcome as rolled back because a group is tagged rolled_back. This was a gap and is fixed in steps 13, 14 and the rollback job.

I do not know who is paged or who the owner is; this is listed under Open questions. On a page the engineer first reads the listener, treats it as the truth, and fixes the tags to match before any new deploy. Added a short 'When a page arrives' section.

questions.text: Step 3 says the run requires the new colour to have 0 instances and stops stray ones. After step 13 or 11a stops a colour, what exactly are its tags, and how does the next run decide which colour is 'new'? Is it purely the opposite of the listener?
questions.about: 3. Read the current state and check it is sane

questions.text: Step 3 requires the live group to be tagged status=live. After a previous deploy, the old colour is tagged retired in step 13 and the new one live in step 10. What tag value does the new colour get in the next deploy's step 6 when it was previously retired, rolled_back or failed? Is it simply overwritten?
questions.about: 6. Start the new release in the idle colour

questions.text: What does the 'migration tool' do when it takes its database lock in step 5, and what happens if a run is aborted or dies mid step 5 while holding that lock? Does the next run get blocked?
questions.about: 5. Apply migrations, once

questions.text: In step 7, who runs the /healthz checks every 10 seconds, and from where? How does the pipeline reach the private addresses of the instances, and what does a pass look like (what response counts)?
questions.about: 7. Health gate: three consecutive passes per instance

questions.text: Step 9 requires all 4 instances to have passed /healthz within the last 10 seconds, but step 7 finished before the smoke suite. Does step 9 run a fresh health check, or reuse the last step 7 result? What if the smoke suite took minutes?
questions.about: 9. Last check before the switch

questions.text: In step 10, how does the listener update stay 'conditional on the listener still pointing at the old one'? Is that a feature of the load balancer API, and what does the run do if the condition fails?
questions.about: 10. Switch: repoint the public listener (one step)

questions.text: Between a rollback (11a or an engineer job) and step 14, the 'old' tag is changed to live. What are the final tags of both groups after an engineer rollback, and does the next deploy's step 3 accept them as sane given the rolled_back group still has tags and 0 instances?
questions.about: Rollback jobs: Rollback while the old colour is still running

questions.text: When the pipeline run ends in Abort, who keeps the failed colour's tag status=failed and what does the next run's step 3 do with that tag? Also in step 14, what does 'marks the tags final' change?
questions.about: 14. Record and release the lock

answers.text: Yes, the new colour is purely the opposite of the listener. After step 13 or 11a its tag is retired, rolled_back or failed with 0 instances. Step 3 checks only the live group's tags and ignores the idle colour's tags, because the listener is the only authority. Added to Terms and step 3.
Yes, step 6 simply overwrites the new colour's tags with status=candidate and release=<sha>, whatever they were before (retired, rolled_back, failed). Written in Terms and step 6.

The migration tool is not chosen. I assume it uses a session-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock to stop two runs migrating at once. Such a lock is released when the connection ends, so a run that dies or is aborted mid step 5 does not block the next run. This is an assumption, not verified, so it is listed under Open questions.

The pipeline job itself runs the checks every 10 seconds from the pipeline runner, which is assumed to be able to reach the instances' private addresses (listed as open). A pass is HTTP 200 from /healthz within 5 seconds. I picked the 5 seconds as a simple limit that fits inside the 10-second interval. Added to Terms and step 7.
Step 9 runs a fresh /healthz check of all 4 instances. Reusing step 7's result would be stale if the smoke suite took minutes. Step 9 wording is fixed.

I assume the load balancer API can make the listener update conditional on the current target. I have not verified that, so it is listed under Open questions. If the condition fails, the listener has moved by itself, and the run stops and pages without touching anything else, as in step 9. Added to step 10.

After an engineer rollback the restored group is tagged live and the group taken out of service is tagged rolled_back, with 0 instances. The next deploy's step 3 accepts that because it checks only the live group's tags and the idle colour has 0 instances. The idle colour's rolled_back tag is overwritten in step 6. Stated in the rollback job and Terms.

The failed colour's status=failed tag simply stays on its target group, written by Abort. The next run's step 3 ignores it and step 6 overwrites it. 'Marks the tags final' did not mean anything extra, because every earlier step already writes its own tags, so I removed that phrase from step 14.

questions.text: Step 3 says it stops stray instances in the new colour, but also 'requires' the new colour to have 0 instances. After stopping them, does it re-check, and what if they will not stop?
questions.about: 3. Read the current state and check it is sane

questions.text: Step 11 uses the new target group's load balancer metrics. Which exact numbers does it read each minute, and how does it exclude pre-switch requests, given the new group got no public traffic before?
questions.about: 11. Watch the 5xx rate for 15 minutes

questions.text: Abort says to stop the 4 new instances and tag failed, but step 5 migrations stay applied. Before the next deploy runs, does anything tell engineers that the database is ahead of the live release?
questions.about: Abort (from step 6, 7 or 8)

questions.text: Step 9 says if the listener has moved by itself, stop and page without touching anything else. What leaves the new instances running then, and who stops them?
questions.about: 9. Last check before the switch

questions.text: In step 10, if the 3 retries fail and the run goes to Abort, but the outcome was unknown (timeout), how does Abort know the listener is really still on the old group before stopping the new instances?
questions.about: 10. Switch: repoint the public listener (one step)

questions.text: The 'rollback after the old colour is shut down' job is a normal deploy with the old SHA. What does it do at step 2 and step 6 for an artifact that was published earlier, and does it go through the same health gate and smoke tests?
questions.about: Rollback jobs: Rollback after the old colour is shut down

questions.text: If an engineer rollback happens after step 11 sees no breach but during the hold, who writes tags and what does the 'old' group's retire_at tag do afterwards? Is retire_at read by anything?
questions.about: 12. Hold the old colour untouched (T0 to T0+30)

answers.text: Yes. Step 3 re-checks the instance count after stopping strays. If the new colour still has instances, the deploy stops and pages. Added to step 3.

Each minute it reads the 5xx count and the total response count for the new target group from the load balancer metrics. It uses only datapoints from T0 onward. Before the switch the group had no public traffic, since all checks went to the instances directly. Written in the Terms.
Only the Abort page. It now says the step 5 migrations stay applied, lists them, and says the database is ahead of the live release. No other mechanism is added.

Nothing stops them automatically, since the listener moved for an unknown reason and the run touches nothing else. The page says the 4 new instances are left running. The engineer decides what to stop, following the page procedure. No new deploy starts until the tags agree with the listener. Added to step 9.

Step 10 reads the listener before each retry. If it points at the new group, the switch worked and the run carries on as success. Abort is reached only when the listener is confirmed on the old group. Abort's trigger now names step 10.

Step 2 is skipped and the artifact already published for that SHA is reused. Step 6 starts instances from it as normal. The run goes through the same health gate and smoke tests. Written in the rollback job.

The rollback job itself writes the tags: restored group live, the other rolled_back. retire_at was not read by anything, so I removed it from step 10. Step 13 uses only switched_at. This is stated in the rollback job.

questions.text: Step 6 sets the tag to candidate and Abort sets failed. But what are the old group's tags during steps 6 to 9: still `live`? And in step 10 the old group becomes `old` and the new one `live`. Is `old` ever read by anything?
questions.about: 6. Start the new release in the idle colour / 10. Switch

questions.text: In step 11, when the run resumes after a crash, how does it know the T0 and the deadline? It says timers are recomputed from `switched_at`. What if the run died between the listener switch and writing `switched_at`? The listener would point at the new group but the tags would not say so.
questions.about: 10. Switch / 11. Watch the 5xx rate (resume rule)

questions.text: In 11a, what does the run do about the 5xx window if the breach happens at the same time as an engineer rollback job starts? Both repoint conditionally, so one of them fails. What does the loser do, and which tags and outcome result?
questions.about: 11a. Automatic rollback / Rollback jobs

questions.text: The lock is held from step 1 for 40 to 50 minutes. What does the 'concurrency group' actually do when a run is waiting and a newer merge arrives? Is the older run reported as cancelled, and is any merge's code ever never deployed? Does the newest run include the older merge's changes?
questions.about: 1. Merge to main starts the run and takes the lock

questions.text: Step 5 runs migrations before the new instances start and any gate. Step 4 only checks that migrations are additive. If a migration is additive but fails halfway through the batch, the first ones stay applied. Does the next deploy's step 4 and 5 see only the remaining ones, and who knows which ones are left?
questions.about: 5. Apply migrations, once

questions.text: In the rollback-after-shutdown job, the run is a normal deploy of the previous SHA. How does an engineer know that SHA and that the old release is safe on the current schema, given step 4 would check migrations not yet applied for that release?
questions.about: Rollback jobs: Rollback after the old colour is shut down

answers.text: During steps 6 to 9 the old group's tags are untouched, so it stays `live` until step 10. Nothing reads `old`; it is only a label for humans (step 13 overwrites it with `retired`). I kept it and said so. Step 6 and the state table now say this.

This was a real gap. Fixed in step 11's resume rule. If the listener is on the old group, the switch never happened and the run restarts from step 3. If the listener is on the new group but the new group has no `switched_at`, the retry writes `switched_at` as now and uses it as T0. That is later than the true switch, so the watch is slightly longer, which is safe. The 10-minute deadline matters only before the switch, so it is not needed on resume.

Both repoints are conditional, so exactly one wins and the loser changes nothing. If 11a loses, it reads the listener, sees it is already on the old group, and carries on with the tags and stopping the failed colour, which are the same values the job writes. If the engineer job loses, it changes nothing, reports 'already rolled back' and exits. Either way the result is old group `live`, new group `rolled_back`, and the run ends as rolled back or failed. Added to 11a and the rollback job.

A waiting run that a newer merge replaces is cancelled and the platform reports it as cancelled. No merge's code is lost, because `main` is one line of history and the newest merge's commit contains all earlier ones, so the newest run deploys everything. Added one sentence to step 1. The exact concurrency-group behaviour is the platform's and was not checked.

Yes. The migration tool's own table is the only record of what was applied. The next deploy's step 4 lists only migrations not recorded there, and step 5 applies only those, so the remaining ones are found automatically. The failure page names the failed migration through the tool's error. Added a clause to step 5.

The engineer reads the previous SHA from the `release` tag on the retired target group. The old release is safe on the current schema because every migration is additive, as step 4 enforced when each was applied. Step 4 for the old release finds nothing pending, since its own migrations were applied long ago, and step 5 is a no-op. Added to the rollback job.

teachbacks.text:
1. Trigger and lock. A merge to `main` completes and starts a pipeline run. The run asks for the lock held in the concurrency group `catalog-web-deploy`. If another run holds it, this one waits. That includes the other run's 30-minute hold. If a newer merge arrives while this run waits, this run is cancelled and the newer one proceeds. Nothing is lost, because the newest merge contains the earlier ones. Nothing in the system has changed yet.

2. Build. With the lock held, the pipeline builds `catalog-web` and the migration bundle and runs the unit tests. It publishes one immutable artifact tagged with the commit SHA. If this fails, the deploy stops and no environment has changed.

3. Read state. The run reads the load balancer listener, which is the only authority on the live colour (blue or green). It treats the other colour as "new". It checks that the live target group is tagged `status=live` with a release, and that the new colour has 0 running instances. Strays are stopped and the count is checked again. On the very first deploy the live group is tagged `live` with release `unknown`. If the listener points at neither group, the tags disagree with the listener, or the strays will not stop, the run stops and pages. Tags on the idle colour are ignored.

4. Check migrations. A static check lists the migrations not yet recorded as applied in the migration tool's PostgreSQL table. It rejects anything that is not additive. Drops, renames, type changes and NOT NULL without a default are rejected. If it fails, the run stops before the database is touched.

5. Apply migrations. The run applies the pending migrations to the shared PostgreSQL database, one transaction each, under the migration tool's lock. If none are pending, it does nothing. If one fails, that migration rolls back its own transaction and earlier ones stay applied. The run stops and pages the owner, naming the failed migration. The live colour keeps serving, because the migrations are additive.

6. Start the new release. The pipeline sends a start request to the platform's instance launcher, naming the artifact SHA. This starts the 10-minute deadline. The launcher starts 4 instances in the new colour and registers them in its target group. The pipeline overwrites the new group's tags with `status=candidate` and `release=<sha>`, and records the start time. The old group's tags stay `live`. If fewer than 4 instances start before the deadline, the run goes to Abort.

7. Health gate. Every 10 seconds the pipeline calls `/healthz` on each new instance's private address. It does not go through the listener, so there is no public traffic. A pass is HTTP 200 within 5 seconds. Each instance needs 3 passes in a row, and one failure resets its count to 0. The gate passes when all 4 are at 3 or more at the same time. If that has not happened by the deadline, the run goes to Abort.

8. Smoke tests. The full smoke suite runs once, with no retry, against the 4 new instances directly. It only gets the time left before the deadline and is killed at the deadline. Any failure or timeout goes to Abort.

9. Last check. The run health-checks all 4 new instances again, confirms the listener still points at the old group, and confirms the deadline has not passed. A failed health check or deadline goes to Abort. If the listener moved by itself, the run stops and pages without touching anything. The new instances are left running and the engineer decides what to stop.

10. Switch. The run makes one listener update from the old group to the new one. The update is conditional on the listener still pointing at the old group. All traffic moves at once. On success the run writes `switched_at` (T0) to both groups, tags the new group `live` and the old group `old`, and reads the listener back to confirm. On a timeout, it reads the listener before acting and before each retry. If the listener is already on the new group, the switch worked. It retries up to 3 times. If the listener is confirmed still on the old group, it goes to Abort. If the condition fails because the listener moved by itself, it stops and pages.

11. Watch. For 15 minutes after T0, the new instances take public traffic. Each minute, starting at T0+5, the run computes the 5xx rate over the trailing 5 minutes. It reads the counts from the new group's load balancer metrics and uses only datapoints from T0 onward. A single window above 1% is a breach. A window with no requests is not a breach. If the metrics cannot be read for 3 consecutive minutes, that counts as a breach.

11a. Automatic rollback, on a breach only. The run repoints the listener back to the old group, conditional on it still pointing at the new one. It tags the old group `live` and the new group `rolled_back`, then stops the failed colour's instances. It skips steps 12 and 13, ends as failed, and pages with the 5xx figures. It retries the repoint 3 times, then pages as an incident. If an engineer's rollback job already moved the listener, the run confirms it is on the old group and carries on with the tags and the stop.

12. Hold. From T0 to T0+30 the old colour keeps its 4 instances, untouched. The lock is still held. An engineer can start a rollback job in this window to repoint the listener at the old colour.

13. Retire the old colour. At 30 minutes after `switched_at`, the run re-reads the listener. If the old group is still not live, it deregisters and stops its 4 instances and tags it `retired`, keeping its `release`. If an engineer's rollback already made the old colour live, it skips the shutdown and the run ends as rolled back. If the shutdown fails, it retries 3 times, then pages. The deploy still counts as done.

14. Record and release. The run reports the outcome (deployed, aborted or rolled back) and releases the lock, so the next queued run can start. If the tags show a `rolled_back` group, the outcome is rolled back. If this step fails, the lock expires with the run. An engineer can release a stuck lock from the pipeline UI after checking the listener against the tags.

Abort, reached from steps 6, 7, 8 and 10. The listener is not touched. The 4 new instances are deregistered and stopped, and the new group is tagged `failed`. The run ends as failed and pages. The page lists the migrations that stay applied and says the database is ahead of the live release. If stopping the instances fails, it retries 3 times, then pages.

If a run dies. The platform's automatic job retry restarts the same run, which keeps the lock (assumed, not verified). The retry reads the listener and the tags. If the listener is on the old group, it restarts from step 3. If the listener is on the new group with no `switched_at`, it writes `switched_at` as now and resumes at step 11. If the listener is on the new group with `switched_at` under 15 minutes ago, it resumes at step 11. Under 30 minutes it resumes at step 12, otherwise at step 13. If it cannot decide, it pages.

Rollback jobs. Both are started by an engineer. While the old colour still runs, the "rollback catalog-web" job repoints the listener, conditional on where it expects it to be. It writes the tags as 11a does and stops the colour it took out of service. After the old colour is shut down, the engineer starts "deploy catalog-web" with the previous release's SHA. That is a normal deploy with the build step skipped. Neither job reverses migrations.

When a page arrives, the engineer checks the listener first and then fixes the tags to match it. No deploy starts until they agree.
gaps: Who is paged and who 'the owner' is. The document says someone must name the alert channel's recipients, and many steps end in a page.

How the launcher starts instances in step 6 and how it gets the artifact. The tool is not named and the document does not say how the launcher is told or how it reports back. Because of that, I cannot say how the pipeline learns that fewer than 4 instances started or when the instances are registered.
What the smoke suite tests and how long it takes. I cannot say how much of the 10-minute deadline remains after the health gate.
How the pipeline detects that the listener 'moved by itself' (steps 9, 10 and 11a) and what could cause it, apart from the rollback jobs.
How the pipeline run waits through the 15-minute watch and 30-minute hold. The document says timers are computed from timestamps, but not whether the run sleeps or polls.

Which step in step 3's 'stray instances' check writes the first-deploy tags relative to an empty listener, and what happens if the listener has no recorded release on later deploys. The document only covers the first deploy.

Whether the job retry in 'If a run dies' keeps the lock, whether the migration tool's lock is released when a run dies, whether the runner can reach the instances' private addresses, and whether the listener update can really be conditional. The document marks all four as assumed, not verified, and the main flow depends on them.

What step 11a does if the metrics cannot be read at the moment it needs the 5xx figures for the page, and how the 'old colour has fewer than 4 healthy instances' check is made, since no health check on the old colour is described.
